title: A Roundup of Jumbo Levi’s® Stories From the Levi Strauss & Co. Archives
summary: Levi Strauss & Co. Historian Tracey Panek shares stories about jumbo pairs of Levi's® jeans from the brand's history.
body_markdown:
Tracey Panek, LS&Co. Historian
Levi Strauss & Co.


September 10, 2026


Most Levi’s® are made to fit the people who wear them. But every now and then, Levi’s® makes a pair so big that the story becomes as memorable as the jeans themselves.


The announcement that Levi Strauss & Co. made a custom pair of[Levi’s® 501® jeans for Big Tex](https://bigtex.com/the-state-fair-of-texas-names-levis-the-official-jeans-of-big-tex/) — the iconic 55-foot-tall cowboy for the 2026 State Fair of Texas — got me thinking about another larger-than-life chapter in Levi’s® history: jumbo Levi’s®.


Long before Big Tex’s 501® jeans, oversized Levi’s® have been turning heads in stores around the world for more than a century. Hanging in windows, stretched across sales floors and occasionally pressed into service as photo props, these supersized jeans were designed to do exactly what they’re still doing today: make people stop, stare and smile.


**From Store Displays to Big Tex**


The history of jumbo Levi’s® comes full circle with Big Tex’s 501® jeans, which have a whopping 382.5-inch waist and nearly 222-inch inseam.


The jeans join a tradition that stretches back more than a century. And judging from the excitement surrounding Big Tex’s new denim, America’s fascination with jumbo Levi’s® isn’t shrinking anytime soon.
